Fact.Name: Your voluntary employee contributions to a qualified retirement plan for 2025
Fact.Description: Form 8880 line 2 column (a): the voluntary employee contributions the primary filer made for 2025 to a qualified retirement plan as defined in section 4974(c), including the federal Thrift Savings Plan. These are after-tax contributions the employee chose to make; no Form W-2 box 12 code carries them, so they are asked here and added to the box 12 elective deferrals on line 2. Question: "Did you make voluntary (after-tax) employee contributions to a qualified retirement plan for 2025? If so, how much?" Help: "Include voluntary employee contributions to a qualified retirement plan, as defined in section 4974(c) (including the federal TSP). Do not include elective deferrals already shown in box 12 of your Form W-2. Contributions designated under section 414(h)(2) (employer pick-up contributions) are treated as employer contributions and are not voluntary employee contributions; do not include them." (2025 Instructions for Form 8880, Line 2). Asked when: the filer said there were contributions not shown on a Form W-2 (/hasSelfReportedContributions) . Unanswered: read as $0 (line 2 is the Form W-2 box 12 total alone), which understates the credit for a filer who has such contributions; nothing is refused. Validation: dollars, not less than $0. Feeds /unfilteredPrimaryFilersDeferralsAndContributions, Form 8880 line 2 column (a).

Fact.Name: Your 2025 ABLE account distributions rolled over to another ABLE account
Fact.Description: The part of the 2025 Form 1099-QA box 1 distributions of the primary filer that was rolled over to an ABLE account within 60 days, so it was not includible in gross income. Question: "Box 1 of your Form 1099-QA includes amounts you intended to roll over to another ABLE account. How much of the 2025 distributions did you roll over to an ABLE account within 60 days?" Help: "Distributions that are not taxable because of a rollover or a trustee-to-trustee transfer are not included on Form 8880 line 4 (2025 Instructions for Form 8880, Line 4). A program-to-program transfer is not in box 1 at all. A return of excess contributions does count." Asked when: a Form 1099-QA of this filer shows a box 1 amount. Unanswered: read as $0, so the whole box 1 reduces line 4 (the credit is not overstated; a filer who did roll over and does not answer gets less credit than the law allows). Validation: dollars, not less than $0 and not more than the box 1 total. Feeds /primaryFiler2025AbleDistributions.

Fact.Name: Form 8880 Credit Limit Worksheet line 2 (credits ordered before the saver's credit)
Fact.Description: Form 8880 Credit Limit Worksheet line 2: the total of the credits Schedule 3 orders ahead of the saver's credit, namely Schedule 3 lines 1 (foreign tax credit), 2 (credit for child and dependent care expenses), 3 (nonrefundable education credits), 6d (credit for the elderly or the disabled) and 6l. It is the same five addends /limitationBasedOnTaxLiability already subtracts, lifted out of that fact's inline Add so the printed worksheet row has a fact of its own; /limitationBasedOnTaxLiability keeps its own arithmetic, so nothing downstream moves. NOTE FOR PROMOTION: this is the SECOND fact in saversCredits to anchor IRC 26, so scripts/test_lint_statute_anchor.py's _GENUINE_26 count and the module's row in scripts/statute_anchor_locked_modules.tsv (which records exactly one 26 co-cite) both need bumping when it lands. 25B cannot serve: former 25B(g) was struck in 2013, so 26(a) is the only section that supplies this ceiling, as the module's own row states.
